`timescale 1ns / 1ps
`default_nettype none

module crc32_d8 (
    input  wire [7:0] data_in,
    input  wire [31:0] state_in,
    output wire [7:0] data_out,
    output wire [31:0] state_out
);
    // Factor the common state/data parity before the CRC matrix.
    wire [7:0] t;
    assign t = state_in[7:0] ^ data_in;

    // Constant evaluation only: contribution of one low-byte basis bit
    // after eight reflected Galois shifts.
    function [31:0] basis;
        input integer bit_index;
        reg [31:0] c;
        integer k;
        begin
            c = 32'h00000001 << bit_index;
            for (k = 0; k < 8; k = k + 1) begin
                if (c[0])
                    c = (c >> 1) ^ 32'hedb88320;
                else
                    c = c >> 1;
            end
            basis = c;
        end
    endfunction

    function [7:0] row_mask;
        input integer row;
        reg [31:0] column;
        integer k;
        begin
            row_mask = 8'b0;
            for (k = 0; k < 8; k = k + 1) begin
                column = basis(k);
                row_mask[k] = column[row];
            end
        end
    endfunction

    function integer count_bits;
        input [7:0] mask;
        integer k;
        begin
            count_bits = 0;
            for (k = 0; k < 8; k = k + 1)
                count_bits = count_bits + mask[k];
        end
    endfunction

    function integer position;
        input [7:0] mask;
        input integer limit;
        integer k;
        begin
            position = 0;
            for (k = 0; k < limit; k = k + 1)
                position = position + mask[k];
        end
    endfunction

    genvar r, b;
    generate
        for (r = 0; r < 32; r = r + 1) begin : rows
            localparam [7:0] MASK = row_mask(r);
            localparam integer N = count_bits(MASK);
            localparam integer EXTRA = (r < 24) ? 1 : 0;
            wire [N+EXTRA-1:0] terms;
            for (b = 0; b < 8; b = b + 1) begin : columns
                if (MASK[b]) begin : selected
                    assign terms[position(MASK, b)] = t[b];
                end
            end
            if (r < 24) begin : shifted_state
                assign terms[N] = state_in[r+8];
            end
            // Compact operands let synthesis balance the parity tree
            // without zero-filled sparse reduction branches.
            assign state_out[r] = ^terms;
        end
    endgenerate

    // These are the actual feedback bits shifted out, not a data bypass.
    assign data_out[4:0] = t[4:0];
    assign data_out[5] = t[5] ^ t[0];
    assign data_out[6] = t[6] ^ t[1];
    assign data_out[7] = t[7] ^ t[2];
endmodule

`default_nettype wire
",
  "bottleneck": "The baseline critical paths traverse input buffering, parity-generation logic, and further output parity logic. Independently reducing state and data operands obscures their common low-byte XOR and increases input loading and parity-network complexity.",
  "rewrite": "Factor t = state_in[7:0] XOR data_in once. Compute the reflected CRC32 byte-update matrix at elaboration using polynomial 0xEDB88320, then build compact parity reductions containing only selected t bits and the applicable shifted upper-state bit. Preserve data_out as the eight successive feedback bits, including the feedback interaction in bits 5 through 7.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to reduce input loading and mapped parity depth relative to the 0.98 ns baseline. A numerical improvement is not established without running the specified mapping and STA flow.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Eight shared input XORs replace repeated state/data participation throughout the matrix. The remaining network consists only of constant-selected parity logic and wires, so area is expected to decrease. Compliance with the 2752.64 um2 cap and zero slew/capacitance violations requires mapped-flow verification.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the crc32_d8 module name and all unsigned port widths; the top has no parameters. Implements the fixed reflected, non-feed-forward CRC32 eight-bit update for arbitrary binary state_in and data_in, without initialization assumptions or final inversion. Both state_out and data_out are fully combinational and defined for every input."
}
